Praise be to God! and There is no God but God; is an offering in testimony of gratitude to God: and ordering any one to act agreeably to the laws, and preventing any one from acting contrary to law, are also so many offerings: and equivalent to all these is performing two Racats in Duha."
units.en2: Abū Dharr narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every morning, an act of charity is due for every joint in your bodies: every 'Glory be to God,' every 'God is greatest,' every 'Praise be to God,' and every 'There is no god but God' counts as charity; enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong count as charity — and two rakʿahs prayed at Ḍuḥā equal all of that."

units.ar: وَعَن أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ وَأَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَا: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " عَنِ اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى أَنَّهُ قَالَ: يَا ابْن آدم اركع لي أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ النَّهَارِ: أَكْفِكَ آخِرَهُ "
units.en: Abudardaa and Abu'd'har Ghaffari said, "the Prophet of God said, verily God said, O sons of Adam! perform four Racats to please me in the beginning of the day, that I may produce your wants in the latter part of it."
units.en2: Abū al-Dardāʾ and Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "God says: O children of Adam, pray four rakʿahs to Me at the beginning of the day, and I will take care of your needs at the end of it."

units.ar: وَعَن بُرَيْدَة قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ: «فِي الْإِنْسَانِ ثَلَاثُمِائَةٍ وَسِتُّونَ مَفْصِلًا فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَتَصَدَّقَ عَنْ كُلِّ مَفْصِلٍ مِنْهُ بِصَدَقَةٍ» قَالُوا: وَمَنْ يُطِيقُ ذَلِكَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: «النُّخَاعَةُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ تَدْفِنُهَا وَالشَّيْءُ تُنَحِّيهِ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْ فَرَكْعَتَا الضُّحَى تُجْزِئُكَ»
units.en: Buraidah said, "I heard the Prophet say, there are three hundred and sixty joints in man; therefore it is incumbent upon him to give alms for every one." The companions said, "O Prophet! who is it can do this?" He said, "cover the water of the throat and nose which may fall in the Masjid, and remove any thorns or filth which may be in the road; and if you cannot do this, perform two Racats in Duha."
units.en2: Burayda narrates: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Man has three hundred and sixty joints, and charity is due for every one of them." The Companions said, "O Prophet, who could manage that?" He said: "Bury the spittle that lands in the mosque, remove thorns or filth from the road — and if you cannot do that, then two rakʿahs at Ḍuḥā suffice."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ صَلَّى الضُّحَى ثِنْتَيْ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً بَنَى اللَّهُ لَهُ قَصْرًا مَنْ ذَهَبٍ فِي الْجَنَّةِ»
units.en: Anas. A. G s. "That person who repeats twelve Racats at Duha, God will build a house for him in paradise."
units.en2: Anas narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever prays twelve rakʿahs at Ḍuḥā, God will build him a house in Paradise."

units.ar: وَعَن معَاذ بن أنس الْجُهَنِيِّ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ قَعَدَ فِي مُصَلَّاهُ حِينَ يَنْصَرِفُ مِنْ صَلَاةِ الصُّبْحِ حَتَّى يُسَبِّحَ رَكْعَتَيِ الضُّحَى لَا يَقُولُ إِلَّا خَيْرًا غُفِرَ لَهُ خَطَايَاهُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ»
units.en: Mua'dh-bin-Anas Juhani. A. G. s. "That person who sits in his place of prayer, from sunrise, till he performs two Racats in Duha, and does not speak in the interim, otherwise than good words, his faults will be pardoned; although they may be like the waves of the sea."
units.en2: Muʿādh ibn Anas al-Juhanī narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever stays in his prayer place from sunrise until he prays two rakʿahs at Ḍuḥā, speaking nothing but good in between, his sins will be forgiven — even if they are like the foam of the sea."

units.ar: وَعَنْ عَائِشَةَ أَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي الضُّحَى ثَمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ تَقُولُ: «لَوْ نُشِرَ لِي أَبَوَايَ مَا تركتهَا»
units.en: Aayeshah. "I used to perform eight Racats in Duha, and would say, if my father and mother could be brought to life by so doing, I would not quit these prayers."
units.en2: ʿĀʾisha narrates that she used to pray eight rakʿahs at Ḍuḥā, and would say: "Even if my father and mother were raised from the dead, I would not give up these prayers."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُصَلِّي الضُّحَى حَتَّى نَقُولَ: لَا يَدَعُهَا وَيَدَعُهَا حَتَّى نَقُولَ: لَا يُصليهَا
units.en: Abu-Sa'id-al-Khud'hri said, "the Prophet used to perform the prayers of Duha some days, till at last we used to say he would never leave them off; and some days he would leave them alone till we would say, he will never say them again."
units.en2: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrates: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the Ḍuḥā prayer for days on end, until we would say he would never leave it; then he would leave it for days, until we would say he would never pray it again.

units.ar: وَعَنْ مُوَرِّقٍ الْعِجْلِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ: تُصَلِّي الضُّحَى؟ قَالَ: لَا. قُلْتُ: فَعُمَرُ؟ قَالَ: لَا. قُلْتُ: فَأَبُو بَكْرٍ؟ قَالَ: لَا. قُلْتُ: فَالنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ؟ قَالَ: لَا إخَاله
units.en: Muwarrik-al-Ijli said to Ibn Omer, "do you say prayers at Duha?" He said, "no." I said, "did Omer-ibn-al-Khat'tab perform them?" He said, "no." I said, "did Abu'bacr?" He said, "no." I said, "did the Prophet of God perform them?" He said, "I do not imagine that he did."
units.en2: Muwarriq al-ʿIjlī narrates: I asked Ibn ʿUmar, "Do you pray Ḍuḥā?" He said, "No." I said, "Did ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb pray it?" He said, "No." I said, "Did Abū Bakr?" He said, "No." I said, "Did the Messenger of God ﷺ pray it?" He said, "I do not think that he did."

sections.heading: On Voluntary Prayers (Matthews, Book IV, Ch. XL)
sections.note: Matthews' chapter XL of his Book IV (On Prayer), printed 1809, pages 285-286. The reports correspond to the Mishkāt's chapter on voluntary prayers (reports 1322-1327); includes the supplications for Istikhārah, Tawbah, and Ḥājah. Matthews omits report 1326.

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِبِلَالٍ عِنْدَ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: «يَا بِلَالُ حَدِّثْنِي بِأَرْجَى عَمَلٍ عَمِلْتَهُ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ دَفَّ نَعْلَيْكَ بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ». قَالَ: مَا عَمِلْتُ عَمَلًا أَرْجَى عِنْدِي أَنِّي لَمْ أَتَطَهَّرْ طَهُورًا فِي سَاعَةِ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ إِلَّا صَلَّيْتُ بِذَلِكَ الطُّهُورِ مَا كُتِبَ لِي أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ
units.en: Abuhurairah. A. G. S. To Billal, at the time of morning prayer, 'O Billal! tell me an act of yours from which you had the greatest hopes; because I heard the noise of your shoes in front of me, in paradise, in the night of my ascension.' Billal said, 'I never did any act besides this, that I said prayers in the divine orders of purification and Wadu.'
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates: At the time of the Fajr prayer, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Bilāl: 'O Bilāl, tell me of the deed you have performed in Islam that brings you the greatest hope, for I heard the sound of your footsteps before me in Paradise.' Bilāl replied: 'I have done nothing of greater hope to me than that whenever I purify myself with ablution at any hour of the night or day, I pray with that purification whatever prayer is decreed for me.'

units.ar: عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُعَلِّمُنَا الِاسْتِخَارَةَ فِي الْأُمُورِ كُلِّهَا كَمَا يُعَلِّمُنَا السُّورَةَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا هَمَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِالْأَمْرِ فَلْيَرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ غَيْرِ الْفَرِيضَةِ ثُمَّ لْيَقُلْ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ فِي عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ - فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ فِي عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ - فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ» قَالَ: «وَيُسَمِّي حَاجَتَهُ»
units.en: Jabir said, 'the Prophet taught me Istikharah; as he did a chapter of the Koran; and he said, when any one of you intends doing any thing, he must perform two Racats expressly for Istikharah: after that, repeat this supplication: "O Lord! I supplicate thy good assistance, in thy great wisdom; and I pray for ability to discern and obtain what is good, through the means of thy power; and I ask a thing of thy munificence: thou knowest, but I do not; thou art powerful, but I am not; thou knowest the absent. O Lord! if thou knowest that the matter which I am about to undertake is good for my religion, my life, and my futurity, then make it easy to me, and give me prosperity in it; and if thou knowest that it is bad for my religion, my life and end, then put it far away from me, and shew me good, wherever it may be; then satisfy me," and the person who prays must then mention the name of his business after these words'.
units.en2: Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh narrates: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us to seek Allah's guidance in all matters (Istikhārah) just as he would teach us a chapter of the Qur'an, saying: 'When any one of you is deliberating on a matter, let him pray two non-obligatory rakʿahs, and then say: O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power, and I ask of Your immense bounty; for You have power and I have none, You know and I know not, and You are the Knower of all unseen things. O Allah, if You know that this matter [and here he names his affair] is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair — or he said: in both this life and the hereafter — then decree it for me, facilitate it for me, and then bless me therein. And if You know that this matter is harmful for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair — or he said: in both this life and the hereafter — then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, and make me pleased with it.'

units.ar: وَعَنْ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَصَدَقَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ: «مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يُذْنِبُ ذَنْبًا ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيَتَطَهَّرُ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ إِلَّا غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ: {وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ}
units.en: Ali-ibn-Abu Talib. Abu'Bakr related to me and spoke truth, saying, 'I heard the Prophet of God say, there is not any man who commits a fault, gets up, and purifies himself, and says his prayers, and asks pardon of God for his offences, but God forgives him. After that he repeated this revelation: "when those who have misbehaved or injured their own souls, either by killing or tyrannizing over others; remember God, and ask pardon for their crimes, God forgives them."'
units.en2: ʿAlī narrates: Abū Bakr told me — and Abū Bakr spoke the truth — that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'There is no person who commits a sin, then rises and purifies himself, prays, and asks forgiveness of Allah, except that Allah forgives him.' Then he recited this verse: {And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins...} (3:135).

units.ar: وَعَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ قَالَ: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا حَزَبَهُ أَمْرٌ صَلَّى
units.en: Hudhaifah said, 'when any mishap befel the Prophet, he would say prayers, and call on God to be relieved from it.'
units.en2: Ḥudhayfah narrates: Whenever a matter distressed or burdened the Prophet ﷺ, he would turn to prayer.

units.ar: وَعَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أَوْفَى قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ كَانَتْ لَهُ حَاجَةٌ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَوْ إِلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ فَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ فَلْيُحْسِنِ الْوُضُوءَ ثُمَّ لِيُصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ لِيُثْنِ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَلْيُصَلِّ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، ثُمَّ لِيَقُلْ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْحَلِيمُ الْكَرِيمُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، أَسْأَلُكَ مُوجِبَاتِ رَحْمَتِكَ وَعَزَائِمَ مَغْفِرَتِكَ وَالْغَنِيمَةَ مِنْ كُلِّ بِرٍّ وَالسَّلَامَةَ مِنْ كُلِّ إِثْمٍ، لَا تَدَعْ لِي ذَنْبًا إِلَّا غَفَرْتَهُ وَلَا هَمًّا إِلَّا فَرَّجْتَهُ وَلَا حَاجَةً هِيَ لَكَ رِضًى إِلَّا قَضَيْتَهَا يَا أَرْحَمَ الرَّاحِمِينَ»
units.en: Abdullah bin Awfa. A. G. S. 'That person who has a want from God or his servants, let him Wadu properly, and then perform two Racats, and speak in the praise of God, and send blessings on the Prophet of God; after which say, "There is no God but God, the clement and beneficent, immaculate God, that God who is Lord of the sublime firmament;" and "I supplicate thee for an act by which I may reach thy mercy, and those dispositions which may be the means of forgiveness of my sins;" and "I supplicate thee for every good; and for safety from every offence; do not allow me to commit any fault, but such as thou wilt pardon; or to suffer any affliction, but such as thou wilt remove; nor any want, but such as thou wilt satisfy; O most compassionate and most merciful!"'
units.en2: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever has a need from Allah or from any of the children of Adam, let him perform ablution properly and pray two rakʿahs, then praise Allah, send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and say: There is no god but Allah, the Clement, the Generous; glory be to Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne; all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I ask of You the requisites of Your mercy, the resolves for Your forgiveness, the spoils of every virtue, and safety from every sin. Leave no sin of mine unforgiven, no anxiety unrelieved, and no need with which You are pleased unfulfilled, O Most Merciful of the merciful!'

sections.heading: On the Prayer Called Tasbīḥ (Matthews, Book IV, Ch. XLI)
sections.note: Matthews' chapter XLI of his Book IV (On Prayer), printed 1809, pages 287-288. The reports correspond to the Mishkāt's chapter on Ṣalāt al-Tasbīḥ (reports 1328-1332); Matthews includes reports 1328, 1330, and 1332.

units.ar: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: لِلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ: «يَا عَبَّاسُ يَا عَمَّاهُ أَلَا أُعْطِيكَ؟ أَلَا أَمْنَحُكَ؟ أَلَا أَحْبُوكَ؟ أَلَا أَفْعَلُ بِكَ عَشْرَ خِصَالٍ إِذَا أَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ ذَلِكَ غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَكَ ذَنْبَكَ أَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ قَدِيمَهُ وَحَدِيثَهُ خَطَأَهُ وَعَمْدَهُ صَغِيرَهُ وَكَبِيرَهُ سِرَّهُ وَعَلَانِيَتَهُ: أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ تَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ وَسُورَةً، فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ مِنَ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي أَوَّلِ رَكْعَةٍ وَأَنْتَ قَائِمٌ قُلْتَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً، ثُمَّ تَرْكَعُ فَتَقُولُهَا وَأَنْتَ رَاكِعٌ عَشْرًا، ثُمَّ تَرْفَعُ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَتَقُولُهَا عَشْرًا، ثُمَّ تَهْوِي سَاجِدًا فَتَقُولُهَا وَأَنْتَ سَاجِدٌ عَشْرًا، ثُمَّ تَرْفَعُ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ السُّجُودِ فَتَقُولُهَا عَشْرًا، ثُمَّ تَسْجُدُ فَتَقُولُهَا عَشْرًا، ثُمَّ تَرْفَعُ رَأْسَكَ فَتَقُولُهَا عَشْرًا، فَذَلِكَ خَمْسٌ وَسَبْعُونَ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ تَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ فِي أَرْبَعِ رَكَعَاتٍ، إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَهَا فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مَرَّةً فَافْعَلْ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَفِي كُلِّ جُمُعَةٍ مَرَّةً، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَفِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مَرَّةً، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَفِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ مَرَّةً، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَفِي عُمْرِكَ مَرَّةً»
units.en: Ibn Abbas. 'Verily the Prophet said to Abbas, "O Abbas! O my uncle! Shall I not give you, shall I not present you, shall I not inform you, of a thing which hides ten faults? When you do it, God will forgive your faults; the first of them and the last of them; and those you did unknowingly, and those you did knowingly; your great and small faults; your disclosed and concealed: it is this, that you perform four Racats, and repeat, in every Racat, the introductory chapter, and any other chapter of the Koran; and when you have done this in the first Racat, say standing, 'O holy God!' and 'praise be to God!' and 'there is no God but God;' and 'God is very great;' fifteen times: after which, perform Rucau and repeat these words at the time, ten times: then raise up your head, and repeat them ten times; then repeat them ten times in your prostration; then raise yourself up and repeat them ten times; then prostrate yourself, and repeat them ten times; then raise up your head, and say them ten times; altogether seventy-five times in every Racat: and do all this in four Racats. If you are able to say these prayers once every day, then do so; but, if not, do it once every Friday: if not, once every month; and, if not, once every year; and, if not able to do it once in every year, then do it once in your life-time."'
units.en2: Ibn ʿAbbās narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said to his uncle ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: 'O ʿAbbās, O uncle! Shall I not give you, shall I not bestow upon you, shall I not confer upon you ten qualities for which, if you perform them, Allah will forgive your sins — the first of them and the last of them, the old and the new, the unintentional and the intentional, the small and the great, the hidden and the manifest? Pray four rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah the Fātiḥah and a surah. When you finish reciting in the first rakʿah while standing, say: Subḥān Allāh, wa al-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa Allāhu Akbar fifteen times. Then bow and say them ten times in rukūʿ; then raise your head from bowing and say them ten times; then go down in prostration and say them ten times; then raise your head from prostration and say them ten times; then prostrate again and say them ten times; then raise your head and say them ten times — that is seventy-five times in every rakʿah. Do this in all four rakʿahs. If you can perform it once every day, do so; if not, then once every Friday; if not, then once a month; if not, then once a year; and if not, then once in your lifetime.'

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلَاتُهُ، فَإِنْ صَلُحَتْ فَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ وَأَنْجَحَ، وَإِنْ فَسَدَتْ فَقَدْ خَابَ وَخَسِرَ، فَإِنِ انْتَقَصَ مِنْ فَرِيضَتِهِ شَيْءٌ قَالَ الرَّبُّ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: انْظُرُوا هَلْ لِعَبْدِي مِنْ تَطَوُّعٍ؟ فَيُكَمَّلُ بِهَا مَا انْتَقَصَ مِنَ الْفَرِيضَةِ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ سَائِرُ عَمَلِهِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah said, 'I heard the Prophet of God say, "verily the first thing which man will be called to give an account of at the resurrection, will be his prayers; and, if they be found good, verily he will find redemption; and, if bad, he will most certainly be forlorn; and if any deficiency be found in his divine prayers, God will say, 'had my servant repeated any of the Nafl prayers? Then the divine would have been completed from the Nafl prayers;' then all his actions will be regulated in this manner."'
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The first matter for which a servant will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection from his deeds is his prayer. If it is sound, he has attained success and prospered; but if it is defective, he has failed and lost. If any shortfall is found in his obligatory prayers, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: See whether My servant has any voluntary (nafl) prayers with which to complete the shortfall in his obligatory ones. Then the rest of his deeds will be reckoned in like manner.'

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا أَذِنَ اللَّهُ لِعَبْدٍ فِي شَيْءٍ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ يُصَلِّيهِمَا، وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ لَيُذَرُّ عَلَى رَأْسِ الْعَبْدِ مَا دَامَ فِي صَلَاتِهِ، وَمَا تَقَرَّبَ الْعِبَادُ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا خَرَجَ مِنْهُ» يَعْنِي الْقُرْآنَ
units.en: Abu-Umamah said, 'A. G. S. "Verily the best of all acts is performing two Racats of prayer; and verily the favours of God are poured down upon the head of his servant as long as he remains at prayers."'
units.en2: Abū Umāmah narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah does not grant a servant permission in anything better than two rakʿahs that he prays; and indeed, righteousness is poured upon the head of the servant as long as he remains in his prayer. Nor do servants draw near to Allah with anything like that which proceeded from Him' — meaning the Qur'an.

sections.heading: On Supplications to God (Matthews, Book IX, Ch. I)
sections.note: Matthews' chapter I of his Book IX, printed 1809, pages 527-532. The reports correspond to the opening chapter of the Mishkāt's Book of Supplications (reports 2223-2260); Matthews omits report 2235.

units.ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ دَعْوَةٌ مُسْتَجَابَةٌ فَتَعَجَّلَ كُلُّ نَبِيٍّ دَعْوَتَهُ وَإِنِّي اخْتَبَأْتُ دَعْوَتِي شَفَاعَةً لِأُمَّتِي إِلَى يومِ القِيامةِ فَهِيَ نَائِلَةٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَنْ مَاتَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي لَا يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "There is a supplication approved for every Prophet; therefore every Prophet supplicated in the world, and met with its approval; and verily I conceal my supplication, for the purpose of asking grace for my sect on the day of resurrection. Then that person will meet with it who has died of my sect, without having associated any thing with God."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every prophet has a supplication that is answered, and every prophet hastened to make his supplication in this world; but I have kept my supplication back as intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection — and it will reach, God willing, whoever of my community dies associating nothing with God."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي اتَّخَذْتُ عِنْدَكَ عَهْدًا لَنْ تُخْلِفَنِيهِ فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ فَأَيُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ آذَيْتُهُ شَتَمْتُهُ لَعَنْتُهُ جَلَدْتُهُ فَاجْعَلْهَا لَهُ صَلَاةً وَزَكَاةً وَقُرْبَةً تُقَرِّبُهُ بِهَا إِلَيْكَ يَوْم الْقِيَامَة»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "O Lord! verily I have entered into a covenant with thee, which shall never be broken; then I am only human, and sometimes am angry with people from my nature; therefore, any Musleman whom I may vex or abuse, curse or beat, then make all these a cause of mercy and of purification of his faults, and of approach to thee, on the day of resurrection."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, I have made a covenant with You, which You never break: I am only human — so whichever believer I hurt, revile, curse, or strike, make that a means of mercy for him, of purification of his faults, and of nearness to You on the Day of Resurrection."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " إِذَا دَعَا أَحَدُكُمْ فَلَا يقُلْ: اللهُمَّ اغفِرْ لي إِنْ شِئتَ ارْحمْني إِنْ شِئْتَ ارْزُقْنِي إِنْ شِئْتَ وَلِيَعْزِمْ مَسْأَلَتَهُ إِنَّه يفعلُ مَا يَشَاء وَلَا مكره لَهُ "
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "When any one of you shall supplicate, then he must not say, O Lord! forgive me if it be thy will; O Lord! have mercy on me if it be thy will; O Lord! give me daily bread if it be thy will; I mean you must not supplicate in a doubtful manner; but with confidence: for verily God doeth what he willeth; there is no compulsion with him."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you supplicates, let him not say, 'O Allah, forgive me if You will; O Allah, have mercy on me if You will; O Allah, provide for me if You will' — he must not supplicate half-heartedly, but with firm resolve, for God does as He wills; nothing compels Him."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " إِذَا دَعَا أَحَدُكُمْ فَلَا يَقُلِ: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي إِنْ شِئْتَ وَلَكِنْ لِيَعْزِمْ وَلْيُعَظِّمِ الرَّغْبَةَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَتَعَاظَمُهُ شيءٌ أعطاهُ "
units.en: Abuhurairah. A. G. s. "When any one of you supplicates, then he must not say, O Lord! forgive me if it be thy will; but, he must be firm and confident in his supplication; because, verily God does not consider what he grants as great, therefore let him supplicate for much."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you supplicates, let him not say, 'O Allah, forgive me if You will'; let him be firm and assured in his supplication, for God does not consider anything He grants too great — so let him ask for much."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «يُسْتَجَابُ لِلْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يَدْعُ بِإِثْمٍ أَوْ قَطِيعَةِ رَحِمٍ مَا لَمْ يَسْتَعْجِلْ» . قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا الِاسْتِعْجَالُ؟ قَالَ: " يَقُولُ: قَدْ دَعَوْتُ وَقَدْ دَعَوْتُ فَلَمْ أَرَ يُسْتَجَابُ لِي فَيَسْتَحْسِرُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَيَدَعُ الدُّعاءَ "
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "God approves the supplication of a servant, so long as he does not ask a thing by which he would be an offender, or break off the connexion of kindred; and so long as he does not ask the immediate performance of his supplication." It was said, "O Prophet! what thing is that?" He said, "being in a hurry is by the supplicator's saying, verily I have supplicated, verily I have supplicated, and have not seen that my supplication is approved; then his hope shall be cut off, and he shall be forlorn, and abandon his supplication."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A servant's supplication is answered so long as he does not ask for something sinful or the severing of kinship, and so long as he does not demand that it happen at once." It was said, "O Prophet, what is that?" He said: "Being in a hurry — the supplicant says, 'I have supplicated and supplicated, and I have not seen my supplication answered' — then his hope is cut off and he gives up supplicating."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " دعوةُ الْمُسْلِمِ لِأَخِيهِ بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ مُسْتَجَابَةٌ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ مَلَكٌ مُوَكَّلٌ كُلَّمَا دَعَا لِأَخِيهِ بِخَيْرٍ قَالَ الْمَلَكُ الْمُوَكَّلُ بِهِ: آمِينَ وَلَكَ بِمِثْلٍ "
units.en: Abu Dardaa. A. G. s. "The supplication of a Musleman for an absent brother is approved, and there is an angel appointed near the head of the supplicator; and whenever he supplicates a good for his brother, the angel says Amen, and says, for thee is the like."
units.en2: Abū al-Dardāʾ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A Muslim's supplication for an absent brother is answered; an angel is appointed at the supplicant's head, and whenever he supplicates good for his brother, the angel says 'Amen — and for you the like.'"

units.ar: وَعَنْ جَابِرٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَا تَدْعُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ وَلَا تدْعُوا على أَوْلَادكُم لَا تُوَافِقُوا مِنَ اللَّهِ سَاعَةً يُسْأَلُ فِيهَا عَطَاءً فَيَسْتَجِيبَ لَكُمْ» . رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ وَذَكَرَ حَدِيثَ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: «اتَّقِ دَعْوَةَ الْمَظْلُومِ» . فِي كِتَابِ الزَّكَاةالْفَصْل الثَّانِي
units.en: Jabir. A. G. s. "Do not supplicate any thing bad for yourselves, nor for your children, nor your property; so that it may not fall in that hour, in which supplications are accepted, and God approves of them."
units.en2: Jābir narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not supplicate against yourselves, nor against your children, nor against your property — lest it fall upon an hour in which supplications are accepted and God answers them."

units.ar: عَنِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ: (وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكم)
units.en: Numan bin Bashir. A. G. s. "To supplicate is worship." After that his highness repeated this verse, God said, "supplicate me, and I will approve."
units.en2: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Supplication is worship." Then he recited the verse: "Your Lord says: Call upon Me, and I will answer you."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "Supplication is the marrow of worship."
units.en2: Anas narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ أَكْرَمَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الدُّعَاءِ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "There is nothing better before God than supplication."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nothing is more honoured before God than supplication."

units.ar: وَعَنْ سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيِّ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَا يَرُدُّ الْقَضَاءَ إِلَّا الدُّعَاءُ وَلَا يَزِيدُ فِي الْعُمْرِ إِلَّا الْبر»
units.en: Salman-Farsi. A. G. s. "Nothing repels calamity but supplication; and age encreases not but in good."
units.en2: Salmān al-Fārsī narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nothing repels calamity but supplication, and nothing increases a life but in goodness."

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِنَّ الدُّعَاءَ يَنْفَعُ مِمَّا نَزَلَ وَمِمَّا لَمْ يَنْزِلْ فَعَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادَ اللَّهِ بِالدُّعَاءِ»
units.en: Ibn-Omer. A. G. s. "Verily supplication is beneficial, in repelling calamity which has descended, and which has not descended; then it is incumbent on you, O servants of God! to supplicate."
units.en2: Ibn ʿUmar narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Supplication helps against calamity that has descended and calamity that has not descended — so it is incumbent on you, servants of God, to supplicate."

units.ar: وَعَنْ جَابِرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يَدْعُو بِدُعَاءٍ إِلَّا آتَاهُ اللَّهُ مَا سَأَلَ أَوْ كَفَّ عَنْهُ مِنَ السُّوءِ مِثْلَهُ مَا لَمْ يَدْعُ بِإِثْمٍ أَوْ قَطِيعَةِ رحم»
units.en: Ja'bir. A. G. s. "There is no one that supplicates for any thing, but God gives it him; or with-holds from him a harm against which he shall have supplicated, so long as he does not supplicate a sin, or tearing asunder affinity."
units.en2: Jābir narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one supplicates for anything without God giving it to him, or turning from him a harm equal to what he supplicated for — so long as he does not supplicate for a sin or the severing of kinship."

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «سَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ وَأَفْضَلُ الْعِبَادَةِ انْتِظَارُ الْفَرَجِ»
units.en: Ibn-Masu'ud. A. G. s. "Supplicate God's munificence; because he loveth to be supplicated; and the best of worshippings is having hopes of redemption from calamity."
units.en2: Ibn Masʿūd narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask of God's bounty, for He loves to be asked; and the best of worship is hope of deliverance from calamity."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ لَمْ يَسْأَلِ اللَّهَ يغضبْ عَلَيْهِ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "He who does not supplicate God, God is angry with."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does not supplicate to God, God is angry with him."

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ فُتِحَ لَهُ مِنْكُمْ بَابُ الدُّعَاءِ فُتِحَتْ لَهُ أَبْوَابُ الرَّحْمَةِ وَمَا سُئِلَ اللَّهُ شَيْئًا يَعْنِي أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ الْعَافِيَةَ»
units.en: Ibn-Omer. A. G. s. "He on whom the doors of supplication shall be opened, for him shall be opened the doors of favor and approval; neither was any thing supplicated of God, which he liked more than supplicating for health."
units.en2: Ibn ʿUmar narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For him whom the doors of supplication are opened, the doors of favour and answer are opened; and nothing was asked of God more beloved to Him than being asked for well-being."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَسْتَجِيبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ عِنْدَ الشَّدَائِدِ فَلْيُكْثِرِ الدُّعَاءَ فِي الرَّخَاءِ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "The person that shall be gladdened, by his supplications being accepted of in a severe disaster, must supplicate very much at other times."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever would be glad to have his supplications answered in times of severe distress should supplicate abundantly at other times."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «ادْعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَنْتُمْ مُوقِنُونَ بِالْإِجَابَةِ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُ دُعَاءً مِنْ قَلْبٍ غَافِلٍ لَاهٍ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "Supplicate of God when ye are certain of its approval; and know that God accepts not the supplication of a negligent heart."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Supplicate to God with certainty of being answered, and know that God does not accept the supplication of a heedless heart."

units.ar: وَعَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِذَا سَأَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ فَاسْأَلُوهُ بِبُطُونِ أَكُفِّكُمْ وَلَا تَسْأَلُوهُ بِظُهُورِهَا»
units.en: Malic-bin-Yes'ar. A. G. s. "When ye supplicate God, do it on the palms of your hands, and not with the backs of them; and when ye have finished supplicating, then draw the palms of your hands over your faces."
units.en2: Mālik ibn Yasār narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you supplicate to God, do it with the palms of your hands, not the backs; and when you have finished supplicating, draw your palms over your faces."

units.ar: وَعَن سَلْمَانَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْرًا»
units.en: Salman. A. G. s. "Verily your patron is ashamed before his servants, when they raise up their hands to him in supplications, to return them empty."
units.en2: Salmān narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your Lord is too generous to turn His servants' hands back empty when they raise them to Him in supplication."

units.ar: وَعَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ فِي الدُّعَاءِ لَمْ يَحُطَّهُمَا حَتَّى يمسح بهما وَجهه
units.en: Omer-ibn-al-Khattab said, "the Prophet used, when he raised up both his hands in supplication, not to bring them down, until he touched his face with them."
units.en2: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrates: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands in supplication, he would not lower them until he touched his face with them.

units.ar: وَعَنْ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا قَالَتْ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَسْتَحِبُّ الْجَوَامِعَ مِنَ الدُّعَاءِ وَيَدَعُ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ
units.en: Aayeshah said, "the Prophet was fond of making supplications which tended to both worldly and future goods; and abandoned such as did not include both."
units.en2: ʿĀʾisha narrates: The Prophet ﷺ loved comprehensive supplications that embrace the goods of this world and the next, and left aside those that did not include both.

units.ar: وَعَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسلم: «إِن أَسْرَعَ الدُّعَاءِ إِجَابَةً دَعْوَةُ غَائِبٍ لِغَائِبٍ»
units.en: Abdullah-bin-Omer. A. G. s. "Verily the quickest supplications for approval are those of the absent for the absent."
units.en2: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The quickest of supplications to be answered is that of the absent for the absent."

units.ar: وَعَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ اسْتَأْذَنْتُ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي الْعُمْرَةِ فَأَذِنَ لِي وَقَالَ: «أَشْرِكْنَا يَا أُخَيُّ فِي دُعَائِكَ وَلَا تَنْسَنَا» . فَقَالَ كَلِمَةً مَا يَسُرُّنِي أَنَّ لِيَ بِهَا الدُّنْيَا. رَوَاهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ وَالتِّرْمِذِيُّ وَانْتَهَتْ رِوَايَتُهُ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ «لَا تنسنا»
units.en: Omer Ibn-al-Khat'tab said, "I asked the Prophet's permission to perform the Omerah; and he permitted me, and said, make us partners, O brother! in your supplications; and do not forget us at that time." Then his highness made use of an expression, which, if I got the whole world, it would not make me so glad.
units.en2: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrates: I asked the Prophet's permission to perform the ʿUmra, and he permitted me and said: "Make us partners, brother, in your supplications; do not forget us." Then he used an expression which — had I been given the whole world — would not have made me gladder.

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " ثَلَاثَةٌ لَا تُرَدُّ دَعْوَتُهُمْ: الصَّائِمُ حِينَ يُفْطِرُ وَالْإِمَامُ الْعَادِلُ وَدَعْوَةُ الْمَظْلُومِ يَرْفَعُهَا اللَّهُ فَوْقَ الْغَمَامِ وَتُفْتَحُ لَهَا أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ وَيَقُولُ الرَّبُّ: وَعِزَّتِي لَأَنْصُرَنَّكِ وَلَوْ بعد حِين "
units.en: Abuhurairah. A. G. s. "There are three persons whose supplications are not denied; one of them a faster, the supplication of whom is not denied at the time of his breaking his fast; the second, a just king; the third, of the oppressed: and God lifts up the supplications of those who suffer under tyranny, upon the clouds; that is, he approves them; and the doors of the regions are opened for them: and God says to the oppressed, I swear by my might, verily I will assist you, although it may be henceforth."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There are three whose supplications are not denied: the faster, whose supplication at the time of breaking his fast is not denied; the just ruler; and the oppressed — God lifts the supplication of the wronged above the clouds, the doors of the heavens are opened for it, and God says: By My might, I will assist you, even if after a while."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " ثَلَاثُ دَعَوَاتٍ مُسْتَجَابَاتٍ لَا شَكَّ فِيهِنَّ: دَعْوَةُ الْوَالِدِ وَدَعْوَةُ الْمُسَافِرِ وَدَعْوَةُ الْمَظْلُومِ "
units.en: Abuhurairah. A. G. s. "There are three supplications approved, in the acceptance of which there is no doubt; one, the supplications of a father for his children, whether for good or ill; the second, the supplications of a traveller, either for himself or others; the third, the supplications of the oppressed."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three supplications are answered beyond all doubt: the supplication of a father for his children — for good or for ill; the supplication of the traveller, for himself or others; and the supplication of the oppressed."

units.ar: عَنْ أَنَسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لِيَسْأَلْ أَحَدُكُمْ رَبَّهُ حَاجَتَهُ كُلَّهَا حَتَّى يَسْأَلَهُ شِسْعَ نَعله إِذا انْقَطع»
units.en: Anas. A. G. s. "You must ask all your wants of God even to the thongs of your shoes, being broken (and in one tradition it is, even to the salt for your pot)."
units.en2: Anas narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask God for all your needs — even to the thong of your shoe when it breaks" (and in one narration: "even to the salt for your pot").

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ فِي الدُّعَاءِ حَتَّى يُرى بياضُ إبطَيْهِ
units.en: Anas said, "the Prophet used to raise up both his hands in supplication, even so that whiteness of his arm-pits was seen."
units.en2: Anas narrates: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands in supplication so high that the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.

units.ar: وَعَن سهل بن سَعْدٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: كَانَ يَجْعَل أصبعيه حذاء مَنْكِبَيْه وَيَدْعُو
units.en: Sameh-bin-Sa'd said, "the Prophet used to raise up his hands, even with his shoulders, and supplicate."
units.en2: Sahl ibn Saʿd narrates of the Prophet ﷺ: He used to raise his hands level with his shoulders when he supplicated.

units.ar: وَعَنِ السَّائِبِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ إِذَا دَعَا فَرفع يَدَيْهِ مَسَحَ وَجْهَهُ بِيَدَيْهِ رَوَى الْبَيْهَقِيُّ الْأَحَادِيثَ الثَّلَاثَة فِي «الدَّعْوَات الْكَبِير»
units.en: Sayib-bin-Yezid relates, from his father, who said, "the Prophet used, when making supplication, to raise up both his hands, and touch his blessed face with them."
units.en2: Al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd relates from his father that when the Prophet ﷺ supplicated, he raised his hands and wiped his blessed face with them.

units.ar: وَعَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: الْمَسْأَلَةُ أَنْ تَرْفَعَ يَدَيْكَ حَذْوَ مَنْكِبَيْكَ أَوْ نَحْوِهِمَا وَالِاسْتِغْفَارُ أَنْ تُشِيرَ بِأُصْبُعٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَالِابْتِهَالُ أَنْ تَمُدَّ يَدَيْكَ جَمِيعًا وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ قَالَ: والابتهالُ هَكَذَا وَرَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ وَجَعَلَ ظُهُورَهُمَا مِمَّا يَلِي وَجْهَهُ
units.en: Acaimah relates Ibn-Augas, who said, "when supplicating it is worthy of you to raise up both your hands even with your shoulders, or near to them; and when asking forgiveness, it is worthy of you to make a sign with one finger; and in weeping, to hold out your arms at full length."
units.en2: ʿIkrima relates from Ibn ʿAbbās: In supplication, raise your hands level with your shoulders or near them; in asking forgiveness, point with one finger; and in earnest entreaty, stretch out your arms at full length.

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ أَنَّهُ يَقُولُ: إِنَّ رَفْعَكُمْ أَيْدِيَكُمْ بِدْعَةٌ مَا زَادَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى هَذَا يَعْنِي إِلَى الصَّدْر
units.en: Ibn-Omer said, "verily your raising up your hands in the way which you do, is an innovation; for the Prophet never raised his higher than his breast."
units.en2: Ibn ʿUmar said: Your raising your hands as you do is an innovation — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never raised his higher than this, meaning to his chest.

units.ar: وَعَنْ أُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا ذَكَرَ أَحَدًا فَدَعَا لَهُ بَدَأَ بِنَفْسِهِ
units.en: Ubai-iss-cab said, "the Prophet used, when remembering any one, to supplicate for him, to begin his supplication for himself, as he would say, O Lord! pardon me and such a one."
units.en2: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrates: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned someone in supplication, he would begin the supplication with himself, saying: "O Lord, pardon me — and so-and-so."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: " مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَدْعُو بِدَعْوَةٍ لَيْسَ فِيهَا إِثْمٌ وَلَا قَطِيعَةُ رَحِمٍ إِلَّا أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ بِهَا إِحْدَى ثَلَاثٍ: إِمَّا أَنْ يُعَجِّلَ لَهُ دَعْوَتَهُ وَإِمَّا أَنْ يَدَّخِرَهَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَإِمَّا أَنْ يَصْرِفَ عنهُ من السُّوءِ مثلَها " قَالُوا: إِذنْ نُكثرُ قَالَ: «الله أَكثر»
units.en: Abu-Sain-Knudum. Verily the Prophet said, "there is no Musleman who may make a supplication, in which is no cause of fault, or cutting off the connexion of kindred, but God will give him one of these three, either he will hasten in the approval of his supplication, that is, gives it in this world; or he preserves his supplication, and hoards it for him, to give in futurity; or removes an ill from him." The companions said, "since we know that supplications are approved in one of these three ways, we will supplicate very much." The Prophet said, "the rewards of God are abundant; your great supplications lessen not his rewards."
units.en2: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said: "No Muslim makes a supplication free of sin and severance of kinship without God granting him one of three things: either He hastens to answer his supplication in this world, or He stores it up for him for the hereafter, or He turns an evil away from him." The Companions said, "Since we know supplications are answered in one of these three ways, we will supplicate very much." The Prophet said, "God's gifts are abundant; your many supplications do not diminish His rewards."

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ " خَمْسُ دَعَوَاتٍ يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُنَّ: دَعْوَةُ الْمَظْلُومِ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِرَ وَدَعْوَةُ الْحَاجِّ حَتَّى يَصْدُرَ وَدَعْوَةُ الْمُجَاهِدِ حَتَّى يَقْعُدَ وَدَعْوَةُ الْمَرِيضِ حَتَّى يَبْرَأَ وَدَعْوَةُ الْأَخِ لِأَخِيهِ بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ ". ثُمَّ قَالَ: «وَأَسْرَعُ هَذِهِ الدَّعْوَات إِجَابَة دَعْوَة الْأَخ لِأَخِيهِ بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ»
units.en: Anas relates, from the Prophet, who said, "there are five supplications which are accepted; one, those of the oppressed, until God takes revenge on the oppressor; the second, those of one intending to make a pilgrimage, until he returns to his own house; the third, those of a combatant with infidels, until he finishes his holy war; the fourth, of a sick person, until restored to health; the fifth, those of a Musleman for his absent brother." After that, his highness said, "the quickest of these supplications in approval, is that of a Musleman for his absent brother."
units.en2: Ibn ʿAbbās narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Five supplications are answered: the supplication of the oppressed until he is vindicated; the supplication of the pilgrim until he returns home; the supplication of the fighter in God's way until he returns; the supplication of the sick until he recovers; and the supplication of a Muslim for his absent brother." Then he said: "The quickest of these to be answered is that of a Muslim for his absent brother."

sections.heading: On Remembering God and Approaching Him (Matthews, Book IX, Ch. II)
sections.note: Matthews' chapter II of his Book IX, printed 1809, pages 533-541. The reports correspond to the remainder of the opening chapter of the Mishkāt's Book of Supplications (reports 2261-2286).

units.ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ وَأَبِي سَعِيدٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَا: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَا يَقْعُدُ قَوْمٌ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا حَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَغَشِيَتْهُمُ الرَّحْمَةُ وَنَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّكِينَةُ وَذَكَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَيْمَنْ عِنْدَهُ»
units.en: Abuhurairah and Abu-Sa'is-Khudum. A. G. s. "No body of people sit, when remembering God, but they are surrounded by angels, which cover them with God's favor; and peace descends upon them, and God remembers them, in that assembly which is near him."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra and Abū Saʿīd narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people sit remembering God without being surrounded by angels, covered in God's favour; peace descends upon them, and God mentions them in the assembly that is near Him."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَسِيرُ فِي طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ فَمَرَّ عَلَى جَبَلٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ: جُمْدَانُ فَقَالَ: «سِيرُوا هَذَا جُمْدَانُ سَبَقَ الْمُفَرِّدُونَ» . قَالُوا: وَمَا الْمُفَرِّدُونَ؟ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ: «الذَّاكِرُونَ الله كثيرا وَالذَّاكِرَات»
units.en: Abu Hurairah said, "the Prophet was coming from Mecca to Medinah, and passed by a mountain called Jumdan, and he said, go quick, this is Jumdan, and Medinah is near. And goers alone went on before; they asked, who are the goers alone, O Prophet?" He said, "they are men who have remembered God very much, and women who have done the same."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was travelling from Mecca to Medina and passed a mountain called Jumdān. He said, "Move on — this is Jumdān, and Medina is near." And those who go alone went ahead. They asked, "Who are those who go alone, O Prophet?" He said: "The men who remember God abundantly, and the women who do the same."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لَا يَذْكُرُ مَثَلُ الْحَيّ وَالْمَيِّت»
units.en: Abu-Musa-Ashari. A. G. s. "The condition of that person who remembers God, and of that who does not, are like the living and the dead; the rememberer is as the living, and the other like the dead."
units.en2: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who remembers God and the one who does not are like the living and the dead: the rememberer is like the living, the other like the dead."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي وَأَنَا مَعَهُ إِذَا ذَكَرَنِي فَإِنْ ذَكَرَنِي فِي نَفْسِهِ ذَكَرْتُهُ فِي نَفْسِي وَإِنْ ذَكَرَنِي فِي مَلَأٍ ذَكَرْتُهُ فِي مَلَأٍ خير مِنْهُم
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. God says, "I am near the hope of my servant who puts it in me; that is, I pardon his sins, when he asks for it; and approve of his repentance, when he repents and turns away from sins; and I accept, when he supplicates; and I am with him, and near him, when he remembers me; when he remembers me in private, I remember him in private, and give him his rewards; and, if he remembers me in a crowd, I remember him in one better than that."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: God says, "I am as My servant hopes of Me: I pardon his sins when he asks; I accept his repentance when he turns from sin; I answer when he supplicates; and I am with him, near him, when he remembers Me — when he remembers Me privately, I remember him privately and reward him; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وأزيد وَمن جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فجزاء سَيِّئَة مِثْلُهَا أَوْ أَغْفِرُ وَمَنْ تَقَرَّبَ مِنِّي شِبْرًا تَقَرَّبْتُ مِنْهُ ذِرَاعًا وَمِنْ تَقَرَّبَ مِنِّي ذِرَاعًا تَقَرَّبْتُ مِنْهُ بَاعًا وَمَنْ أَتَانِي يَمْشِي أَتَيْتُهُ هَرْوَلَةً وَمَنْ لَقِيَنِي بِقُرَابِ الْأَرْضِ خَطِيئَةً لَا يُشْرِكُ بِي شَيْئًا لَقِيتُهُ بِمِثْلِهَا مَغْفِرَةً "
units.en: Abu Dhar Ghaffari. A. G. s. Almighty God says, "he who does one good act, for him are ten rewards; and I also give more to whomever I will; and he who does an ill, its retaliation is equal to it, or I forgive him; and he who seeks to approach me one span, I will seek to approach one cubit; and he who seeks to approach me one cubit, I will seek to approach him two fathoms; and he who walks towards me, I will run towards him; and he who comes before me with the earth full of sins, and does not associate any thing with me, I will come before him with a front of forgiveness like that."
units.en2: Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Almighty God says, "Whoever does one good deed has ten rewards — and I give more to whom I will; and whoever does an evil deed is repaid only with its like, or I forgive him. Whoever draws near Me a span, I draw near him a cubit; whoever draws near Me a cubit, I draw near him two fathoms; whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running; and whoever comes before Me with an earth-full of sins, having associated nothing with Me, I come before him with an equal front of forgiveness."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى قَالَ: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ وَمَا تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيَّ عَبْدِي بِشَيْءٍ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا افْتَرَضْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَمَا يَزَالُ عَبْدِي يَتَقَرَّبُ إِلَيَّ بِالنَّوَافِلِ حَتَّى أُحِبَّهُ فَإِذَا أَحْبَبْتُهُ كُنْتُ سَمْعَهُ الَّذِي يَسْمَعُ بِهِ وَبَصَرَهُ الَّذِي يُبْصِرُ بِهِ وَيَدَهُ الَّتِي يَبْطِشُ بِهَا وَرِجْلَهُ الَّتِي يَمْشِي بِهَا وَإِنْ سَأَلَنِي لَأُعْطِيَنَّهُ وَلَئِنِ اسْتَعَاذَنِي لَأُعِيذَنَّهُ وَمَا تَرَدَّدْتُ عَنْ شَيْءٍ أَنَا فَاعِلُهُ تَرَدُّدِي عَنْ نَفْسِ الْمُؤْمِنِ يَكْرَهُ الْمَوْتَ وَأَنَا أَكْرَهُ مُسَاءَتَهُ وَلَا بُدَّ لَهُ مِنْهُ "
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. God said, "Whoever considers as an enemy one of my friends, verily I will denounce against him war and enmity: and whoever seeks to approach me by that which I have given as my divine commands, is most loved by me: and my servant is always seeking to approach me by Sunnat; so that I love him; therefore, when I hold him as a friend, I am his hearing by which he hears, and I am his sight by which he sees, and I am his hands by which he holds, and I am his feet by which he walks: if this servant supplicates me, verily I give unto him; and, if he seeks protection with me from harm and ills, I give him protection; and I do not hesitate about any thing in which I am the doer; like my hesitation in taking the soul of a Momin, who dislikes death; and I dislike making him sad; but there is no remedy for him against death; that is, I (on account of the regard I have for my servant) hesitate about causing him to die, because he is displeased at death; but there is no remedy for it; he certainly must die."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: God said, "Whoever treats a friend of Mine as an enemy, I declare war on him. Nothing draws My servant near to Me like what I have commanded; and My servant keeps drawing near to Me through extra works until I love him — and when I love him, I am his hearing by which he hears, his sight by which he sees, his hand by which he holds, and his feet by which he walks. If he asks Me, I give him; if he seeks My protection, I protect him. And I never hesitate in anything I do as I hesitate to take the soul of a believer who dislikes death — I dislike displeasing him, yet there is no escape from it: he must die."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: " إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً يَطُوفُونَ فِي الطُّرُقِ يَلْتَمِسُونَ أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ فَإِذَا وَجَدُوا قَوْمًا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ تَنَادَوْا: هَلُمُّوا إِلَى حَاجَتِكُمْ " قَالَ: «فَيَحُفُّونَهُمْ بِأَجْنِحَتِهِمْ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا» قَالَ: " فَيَسْأَلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ: مَا يَقُولُ عِبَادِي؟ " قَالَ: " يَقُولُونَ: يُسَبِّحُونَكَ وَيُكَبِّرُونَكَ وَيُحَمِّدُونَكَ وَيُمَجِّدُونَكَ " قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُ: هَلْ رَأَوْنِي؟ " قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُونَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ مَا رَأَوْكَ " قَالَ فَيَقُولُ: كَيْفَ لَوْ رَأَوْنِي؟ قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُونَ: لَوْ رَأَوْكَ كَانُوا أَشَدَّ لَكَ عِبَادَةً وَأَشَدَّ لَكَ تَمْجِيدًا وَأَكْثَرَ لَكَ تَسْبِيحًا " قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُ: فَمَا يَسْأَلُونَ؟ قَالُوا: يسألونكَ الجنَّةَ " قَالَ: " يَقُول: وَهل رأوها؟ " قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُونَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَبِّ مَا رَأَوْهَا " قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُ: فَكَيْفَ لَوْ رَأَوْهَا؟ " قَالَ: " يقولونَ: لَو أنَّهم رأوها كَانُوا أَشد حِرْصًا وَأَشَدَّ لَهَا طَلَبًا وَأَعْظَمَ فِيهَا رَغْبَةً قَالَ: فممَّ يتعوذون؟ " قَالَ: " يَقُولُونَ: مِنَ النَّارِ " قَالَ: " يَقُولُ: فَهَلْ رَأَوْهَا؟ " قَالَ: يَقُولُونَ: «لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَبِّ مَا رَأَوْهَا» قَالَ: " يَقُولُ: فَكَيْفَ لَوْ رَأَوْهَا؟ " قَالَ: «يَقُولُونَ لَوْ رَأَوْهَا كَانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهَا فِرَارًا وَأَشَدَّ لَهَا مَخَافَةً» قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُ: فَأُشْهِدُكُمْ أَنِّي قَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَهُمْ " قَالَ: " يَقُولُ مَلَكٌ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: فِيهِمْ فُلَانٌ لَيْسَ مِنْهُمْ إِنَّمَا جَاءَ لِحَاجَةٍ قَالَ: هُمُ الْجُلَسَاءُ لَا يَشْقَى جَلِيسُهُمْ " قَالَ: فَكَيْفَ لَوْ رَأَوْا نَارِي؟ قَالُوا: يَسْتَغْفِرُونَكَ " قَالَ: " فَيَقُولُ: قَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَهُمْ فَأَعْطَيْتُهُمْ مَا سَأَلُوا وَأَجَرْتُهُمْ مِمَّا اسْتَجَارُوا " قَالَ: " يَقُولُونَ: رَبِّ فِيهِمْ فُلَانٌ عَبْدٌ خَطَّاءٌ وَإِنَّمَا مَرَّ فَجَلَسَ مَعَهُمْ " قَالَ: «فَيَقُولُ وَلَهُ غَفَرْتُ هم الْقَوْم لَا يشقى بهم جليسهم»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "Verily there are angels which move around houses for God, and seek for the rememberers of God; and when they find an assembly remembering God, they say to one another, come ye, to that which ye were seeking. Then the angels cover the repeaters of God's name with wings, as far as the lowest region (called the region of the world)." The Prophet said, "when the angels go to the court of God, God asks them, (while knowing better than they) what do my servants say and do? Then the angels say, they remember thee with purity, greatness, praise, and respect. And God says, have they seen me? The angels say, no by God, they have not seen thee. Then God says, what would their condition be if they had seen me? The angels say, if they had seen thee, they would be more strenuous in worshipping thee, and in holding thee mighty and glorious; and they would be more excessive in repeating thy immaculate attributes. God says, then what do they ask? The angels say, paradise. Then God says, have they seen paradise? The angels say, we swear by God they have not; that is, their belief in paradise is mysterious. Then God says, what would their state have been had they seen paradise? The angels say, if they had seen paradise, they would be very ambitious for it; and would be excessive wishers of it, and very great desirers of it. God says, what thing is it they seek protection from? The angels say, from hell fire. God says, have they seen the fire? The angels say, no; if they had seen the fire, they would be greater runners from it. God says, how would they have been, had they seen the fire? The angels say, if they had seen the fire, they would be great runners from it, and would be greater fearers of it. Then God says, I take ye as evidences; that verily I have pardoned them. One of the angels says, there is a person amongst them who is not a rememberer of thee, and is only come on account of his own needs. God says, verily it is not unfortunate for him to sit in such an assembly as this, although he may have come on any other account."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "God has angels who travel about seeking the rememberers of God, and when they find an assembly remembering Him, they call to one another, 'Come to what you were seeking.' They cover them with their wings up to the lowest heaven. When the angels return, God asks them — though He knows better — 'What are My servants saying and doing?' They say, 'They glorify You, magnify You, praise You, and revere You.' God says, 'Have they seen Me?' They say, 'No, by God, they have not seen You.' He says, 'How would they be if they had seen Me?' They say, 'Had they seen You, they would be more fervent in worship, more in magnifying and glorifying You.' He says, 'What do they ask?' They say, 'Paradise.' He says, 'Have they seen it?' They say, 'No, by God.' He says, 'How would they be if they had seen it?' They say, 'They would long for it more and desire it more.' He says, 'What do they seek refuge from?' They say, 'The Fire.' He says, 'Have they seen it?' They say, 'No — had they seen it, they would flee from it harder and fear it more.' God says, 'I call you to witness that I have pardoned them.' One angel says, 'Among them is someone who is not a rememberer of You; he only came for a need of his own.' God says, 'It is no misfortune for him to sit in such an assembly, whatever he came for — the companions of such an assembly are not made wretched."

units.ar: وَعَن حَنْظَلَة بن الرّبيع الأسيدي قَالَ: لَقِيَنِي أَبُو بكر فَقَالَ: كَيْفَ أَنْتَ يَا حَنْظَلَةُ؟ قُلْتُ: نَافَقَ حَنْظَلَةُ قَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ مَا تَقُولُ؟ قُلْتُ: نَكُونُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُذَكِّرُنَا بِالنَّارِ وَالْجَنَّةِ كَأَنَّا رَأْيُ عَيْنٍ فَإِذَا خَرَجْنَا مِنْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَافَسْنَا الْأَزْوَاجَ وَالْأَوْلَادَ وَالضَّيْعَاتِ نَسِينَا كثيرا قَالَ أَبُو بكر: فو الله إِنَّا لَنَلْقَى مِثْلَ هَذَا فَانْطَلَقْتُ أَنَا وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ حَتَّى دَخَلْنَا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقُلْتُ: نَافَقَ حَنْظَلَةُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «وَمَا ذَاكَ؟» قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ نَكُونُ عِنْدَكَ تُذَكِّرُنَا بِالنَّارِ وَالْجَنَّةِ كَأَنَّا رَأْيَ عَيْنٍ فَإِذَا خَرَجْنَا مِنْ عِنْدِكَ عَافَسْنَا الْأَزْوَاجَ وَالْأَوْلَادَ وَالضَّيْعَاتِ نَسِينَا كَثِيرًا فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «الَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَوْ تَدُومُونَ عَلَى مَا تَكُونُونَ عِنْدِي وَفِي الذِّكْرِ لَصَافَحَتْكُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ عَلَى فُرُشِكُمْ وَفِي طُرُقِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَا حَنْظَلَةُ سَاعَةٌ وَسَاعَةٌ» ثَلَاث مَرَّات
units.en: Handhalah-ibn-al-Rubaiya-Usaid said, "Abubacr came to me and said, how are you? What state are you in the truth of faith, O Handhalah?" I said, "I am become an hypocrite." Abubakr said, "immaculate God! how do you ascribe hypocrisy to yourself?" I said, "we stay near the Prophet when he reminds us of hell and paradise, that you might say we see them with our eyes; and when we leave him, we mix with our wives and children, and are engaged in our fields and gardens." Ab'ubakr said, "I swear by God, verily I myself am in these predicaments which you mention." And Abu Bakr went to the Prophet and said, "we are become hypocrites, O Prophet! that is, in all cases our internal does not accord with our external." The Prophet said, "what is this, and on what account do ye ascribe hypocrisy to yourselves?" We said, "O messenger of God! we stay near you when you remind us of hell and paradise, as if we saw them with our eyes; and when we leave you, we mix with our women and children, attend to our fields and gardens, and forget a great deal of what we remembered with you." The Prophet said, "I swear by him in whose mighty hands is my life, that if you were always to remain in the state in which you are when with me, and when remembering God, verily the angels would shake you by the hand upon your beds, and come before you and take you by the hand in your roads; that is, you would always meet with angels; but O Handhalah! be one said in remembering God, and the performance of his duties; and another in the performance of your duty to your family." This he repeated thrice.
units.en2: Ḥanẓala ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Usaydī narrates: Abū Bakr met me and said, "How are you, Ḥanẓala?" I said, "I have become a hypocrite." Abū Bakr said, "God is immaculate — why do you call yourself a hypocrite?" I said, "When we are with the Prophet, he reminds us of Hell and Paradise until it is as if we see them with our eyes; but when we leave him, we mix with our wives and children and get busy with our fields and gardens." Abū Bakr said, "By God, I am in the same condition you describe." He went to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "We have become hypocrites, O Prophet — our inward does not match our outward." The Prophet said, "What is this? Why do you call yourselves hypocrites?" We said, "O Messenger of God, when we are with you, you remind us of Hell and Paradise as if we saw them with our eyes; when we leave you, we mix with our families and forget much of what we remembered with you." The Prophet said, "By Him in whose hand is my life — if you always remained as you are when with me and when remembering God, the angels would shake your hands on your beds and on your roads; but, Ḥanẓala — an hour for remembering God and His duties, and an hour for your duty to your family." He repeated this three times.

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «أَلَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرِ أَعْمَالِكُمْ وَأَزْكَاهَا عِنْدَ مَلِيكِكُمْ؟ وَأَرْفَعِهَا فِي دَرَجَاتِكُمْ؟ وَخَيْرٍ لَكُمْ مِنْ إِنْفَاقِ الذهبِ والوَرِقِ؟ وخيرٍ لكم مِنْ أَنْ تَلْقَوْا عَدُوَّكُمْ فَتَضْرِبُوا أَعْنَاقَهُمْ وَيَضْرِبُوا أَعْنَاقَكُمْ؟» قَالُوا: بَلَى قَالَ: «ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ»
units.en: Abu Dardaa. A. G. s. "Shall I not inform you of the best of your actions? shall I not inform you of your purest actions before your king (i. e. God?) Shall I not inform you of your most exalted actions in your stations, and better for you than spending gold and silver? Shall I not inform you of an action which is better for you, than fighting with infidels, and cutting off their heads, and their cutting off yours?" The companions said, "yes, inform us." The Prophet said, "these actions are remembering God."
units.en2: Abū al-Dardāʾ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I tell you of the best of your actions — the purest before your King, the most exalting of your ranks, better for you than spending gold and silver, and better for you than fighting the enemy, you cutting off their heads and they cutting off yours?" The Companions said, "Yes, tell us." The Prophet said, "It is the remembrance of God."

units.ar: وَعَن عبد الله بن يسر قَالَ: جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: أَيُّ النَّاسِ خَيْرٌ؟ فَقَالَ: «طُوبَى لِمَنْ طَالَ عُمْرُهُ وَحَسُنَ عَمَلُهُ» قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيُّ الْأَعْمَالِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ: ( «ن تُفَارِقَ الدُّنْيَا وَلِسَانُكَ رَطْبٌ مِنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ»
units.en: Abdullah-bin-Bushr said, "an Aarabi came to the Prophet and asked, which is the best of men?" The Prophet said, "joy be to that person whose life is long, and actions good; I mean, this is the best of men." The Aarabi said, "O Prophet! which is the best of actions, and the most rewarded?" He said, "the best of actions is this, that you separate from the world, and die whilst your tongue is moist in repeating the name of God."
units.en2: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yusr narrates: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked, "Which of men is best?" The Prophet said, "Glad tidings to the one whose life is long and whose deeds are good — that is the best of men." The Bedouin said, "O Prophet, which deed is best and most rewarded?" He said, "The best of deeds is that you part from this world and die with your tongue moist in the remembrance of God."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَنَسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِذَا مَرَرْتُمْ بِرِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ فَارْتَعُوا» قَالُوا: وَمَا رِيَاضُ الْجِنّ؟ قَالَ: «حلق الذّكر»
units.en: Anas. A. G. s. "When you pass through the gardens of paradise, eat." The companions said, "what are the gardens of paradise?" The Prophet said, "the gardens of paradise are the circles of those who make mention of God."
units.en2: Anas narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you pass through the gardens of Paradise, graze." They said, "What are the gardens of Paradise?" The Prophet said: "The circles of those who make mention of God."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَنْ قَعَدَ مَقْعَدًا لَمْ يَذْكُرِ اللَّهَ فِيهِ كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ تِرَةٌ وَمَنِ اضْطَجَعَ مَضْجَعًا لَا يذكر الله فِيهِ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ تِرَةٌ»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "The person who sits in an assembly, and does not remember God, shame and loss will be for him on the day of resurrection; and he who falls upon his side in his place of sleep, and does not remember God therein, shame and loss will be on him from God on the resurrection; that is, in every situation, sitting, standing, asleep and awake, night and day, be employed in the remembrance of God: every time that passes without it will be a cause of shame and loss at the resurrection."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever sits in an assembly and does not remember God, shame and loss will be his on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever lies down on his side in his sleeping-place and does not remember God, shame and loss from God will be his at the Resurrection — that is: in every state, sitting, standing, asleep or awake, night and day, be employed in the remembrance of God; every moment passed without it will be a cause of shame and loss at the Resurrection."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا مِنْ قَوْمٍ يَقُومُونَ مِنْ مَجْلِسٍ لَا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ فِيهِ إِلَّا قَامُوا عَنْ مِثْلِ جِيفَةِ حِمَارٍ وَكَانَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسرَةً»
units.en: Abu Hurairah. A. G. s. "There is no assembly, which rises up from the place of sitting, without remembering God therein, but rises up like as from dead asses; and it will be a means of shame and loss to them."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No assembly rises from its sitting-place without remembering God therein, except that it rises as if from a dead ass — and it will be a cause of shame and loss to them."

units.ar: وَعَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا جَلَسَ قَوْمٌ مَجْلِسًا لَمْ يَذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ فِيهِ وَلَمْ يُصَلُّوا عَلَى نَبِيِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانَ عَلَيْهِمْ تِرَةً فَإِنْ شَاءَ عَذَّبَهُمْ وَإِنْ شَاءَ غَفَرَ لَهُمْ»
units.en: Ab'uhurairah. A. G. s. "No tribe sits in a place, in which they do not remember God, and send grace upon his Prophet, but will be ashamed, and lose, on the day of resurrection; and, if God wills, he will punish them; and, if he please, he will pardon them."
units.en2: Abū Hurayra narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people sit in a place without remembering God and sending blessings upon His Prophet, except that they will be ashamed and lose on the Day of Resurrection — then if God wills He punishes them, and if He pleases He pardons them."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أُمِّ حَبِيبَةَ قَالَتْ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «كُلُّ كَلَامِ ابْنِ آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ لَا لَهُ إِلَّا أَمْرٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ نَهْيٌ عَنْ مُنْكَرٍ أَوْ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ»
units.en: Omm-Habibah. A. G. s. "Every speech of man is a loss to him, not a gain; except ordering anyone to obey the laws, or with-holding anyone from that which is unlawful, or remembering God."
units.en2: Umm Ḥabība narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every word of man is a loss to him, not a gain — except enjoining what is lawful, forbidding what is unlawful, or remembering God."

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَا تُكْثِرُوا الْكَلَامَ بِغَيْرِ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ كَثْرَةَ الْكَلَامِ بِغَيْرِ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ قَسْوَةٌ لِلْقَلْبِ وَإِنَّ أَبْعَدَ النَّاسِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْقَلْبُ الْقَاسِي»
units.en: Ibn-Omer. A. G. s. "Talk not much without remembering God, because verily it is a cause of hardness of heart; and verily the farthest man from God is the hard hearted."
units.en2: Ibn ʿUmar narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not talk much without remembering God, for it hardens the heart — and the farthest of men from God is the hard-hearted."

units.ar: وَعَنْ ثَوْبَانَ قَالَ: لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ (وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَب وَالْفِضَّة) كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي بَعْضِ أَسْفَارِهِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِهِ: نَزَلَتْ فِي الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ لَوْ عَلِمْنَا أَيُّ الْمَالِ خَيْرٌ فَنَتَّخِذَهُ؟ فَقَالَ: «أَفْضَلُهُ لِسَانٌ ذَاكِرٌ وَقَلْبٌ شَاكِرٌ وَزَوْجَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ تُعِينُهُ عَلَى إِيمَانِهِ»
units.en: Thawi'an said, "when this revelation came down, those who treasure up gold and silver, and do not expend them in the road of God, the gold and silver will be heated in hellfire, and their foreheads, sides and backs will be marked with them, we were with the Prophet, in some of his journeys; and some of his highness' companions said, this revelation is come down in denunciation against gold and silver; would to God! that we knew what property is better than gold and silver, we would take it and lay it by." Then his highness said, "The best of property is a remembering tongue and grateful heart; and the wife of a Musleman, who assists him in faith."
units.en2: Thawbān narrates: When the verse came down — "those who treasure up gold and silver and do not spend them in God's way" — we were with the Prophet on one of his journeys, and some of his companions said, "This revelation has come down denouncing gold and silver; would that we knew what property is better than gold and silver, we would take it and store it up." Then the Prophet said: "The best of property is a remembering tongue and a grateful heart — and a Muslim wife who assists her husband in faith."

units.ar: عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ مُعَاوِيَةُ عَلَى حَلْقَةٍ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ: مَا أَجْلَسَكُمْ؟ قَالُوا: جَلَسْنَا نَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ قَالَ: آللَّهِ مَا أَجْلَسَكُمْ إِلَّا ذَلِكَ؟ قَالُوا: آللَّهِ مَا أَجْلَسَنَا غَيْرُهُ قَالَ: أما إِنِّي لم أستحلفكم تُهْمَة لكم وَمَا كَانَ أَحَدٌ بِمَنْزِلَتِي مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَقَلَّ عَنْهُ حَدِيثًا مِنِّي وَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ خَرَجَ عَلَى حَلْقَةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ: «مَا أَجْلَسَكُمْ هَاهُنَا» قَالُوا: جَلَسْنَا نَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ وَنَحْمَدُهُ عَلَى مَا هَدَانَا لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَنَّ بِهِ علينا قَالَ: " آالله مَا أجلسكم إِلَّا ذَلِك؟ قَالُوا: آالله مَا أَجْلَسَنَا إِلَّا ذَلِكَ قَالَ: «أَمَا إِنِّي لَمْ أَسْتَحْلِفْكُمْ تُهْمَةً لَكُمْ وَلَكِنَّهُ أَتَانِي جِبْرِيلُ فَأَخْبَرَنِي أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يُبَاهِي بِكُمُ الْمَلَائِكَة»
units.en: Abu Sa'id Khudri said, "Muawiah came to an assembly that was sitting in a circle in the Masjid, and said, what has caused you to sit here; and why do you do so?" They said, "we are sitting remembering God." He said, "by God are you not sitting otherwise than in the remembrance of God?" They said, "we swear by God nothing else has caused our sitting." Muawiah said, "beware; verily I did not take an oath from you, on account of suspecting you of falsehood, but expressly in imitation of the Prophet; for verily he came to a circle of his companions, and said, what has caused you to sit here?" They said, "the remembrance of God, and we praise him for his shewing us the road to Islam, and for his benefiting us by it." His highness said, "by God has nothing else caused your sitting?" They said, "by God we swear, nothing besides." The Prophet said, "beware! verily I did not take an oath from you on suspicion of falsehood; but Gabriel came to me, and informed me, saying, God honours his angels by you."
units.en2: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrates: Muʿāwiya came out to a circle sitting in the mosque and said, "What made you sit here?" They said, "We are sitting remembering God." He said, "By God — are you sitting for nothing else?" They said, "By God, nothing else made us sit." Muʿāwiya said, "Mind — I did not make you swear because I suspected you of lying, but only in imitation of the Prophet ﷺ: he came upon a circle of his companions and said, 'What made you sit here?' They said, 'The remembrance of God; we praise Him for showing us the road to Islam and blessing us with it.' He said, 'By God — nothing else made you sit?' They said, 'By God, we swear, nothing else.' The Prophet said, 'Mind — I did not make you swear out of suspicion; but Gabriel came to me and told me that God boasts of you to His angels.'"

units.ar: وَعَن عبد الله بن يسر: أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ شَرَائِعَ الْإِسْلَامِ قَدْ كَثُرَتْ عَلَيَّ فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِشَيْءٍ أَتَشَبَّثُ بِهِ قَالَ: " لَا يَزَالُ لِسَانُكَ رَطْبًا بِذكر اللَّهِ)
units.en: Abdullah-bin-Busr said, "verily, a man said, O messenger of God! really the rules of Islam are many upon me; then inform me a thing, by which I may lay hold; I mean, inform me of an act by the doing of which I may obtain great rewards." His highness said, "let your tongue be always moist in the remembrance of God."
units.en2: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yusr narrates: A man said, "O Messenger of God, the laws of Islam have become many for me — tell me of one thing to hold fast to, a deed by which I may gain great reward." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of God."

units.ar: وَعَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ سُئِلَ: أَيُّ الْعِبَادِ أَفْضَلُ وَأَرْفَعُ دَرَجَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ؟ قَالَ: «الذَّاكِرُونَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَالذَّاكِرَاتُ» قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمِنَ الْغَازِي فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: «لَوْ ضَرَبَ بِسَيْفِهِ فِي الْكُفَّارِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ حَتَّى يَنْكَسِرَ وَيَخْتَضِبَ دَمًا فَإِنَّ الذَّاكِرَ لِلَّهِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْهُ دَرَجَة»
units.en: Abu-Sa'id-Khudri said, "verily the messenger of God was asked, what servant is the best, and of highest station, near God, on the day of resurrection?" He said, "men and women, great rememberers of God." It was said, "O Prophet! are repeaters of God's name also better, and of higher degree, than the combatants in the cause of God?" He said, "a combatant, if he draws his sword against the infidels and polytheists, even until it be broken, and the combatant or his sword be smeared in blood, still surely the rememberer of God is better."
units.en2: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrates: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked, "Which servant is best and of highest station near God on the Day of Resurrection?" He said, "Men and women who remember God abundantly." It was said, "O Prophet, are the rememberers of God really better and higher in degree than the fighters in God's cause?" He said, "If a fighter draws his sword against the unbelievers until it breaks, smeared in blood — still, the rememberer of God is better."

units.ar: وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «الشَّيْطَانُ جَاثِمٌ عَلَى قَلْبِ ابْنِ آدَمَ فَإِذَا ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ خَنَسَ وَإِذا غفَلَ وسوس»
units.en: Ibn-Abbas. A. G. s. "The devil is a sitter upon the heart of man; therefore, when man remembers God, it separates the devil; and when he is negligent and remiss in the remembrance of God, he throws bad machinations into the heart of man."
units.en2: Ibn ʿAbbās narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Satan sits upon the heart of man: when man remembers God, Satan withdraws; and when he is heedless of remembering God, Satan casts his evil whispers into his heart."

units.ar: وَعَنْ مَالِكٍ قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يَقُولُ: «ذَاكِرُ اللَّهِ فِي الْغَافِلِينَ كَالْمُقَاتِلِ خَلْفَ الْفَارِّينَ وَذَاكِرُ اللَّهِ فِي الْغَافِلِينَ كَغُصْنٍ أَخْضَرَ فِي شَجَرٍ يَابِس»
units.en: Matic said, "it reached me that the Prophet was wont to say, a rememberer of God amongst the negligent, is like a fighter after the runners away; and a rememberer amongst the negligent, is as a green branch on a dry tree."
